# opnsense_haproxy_frontend (Data Source)

HAProxy frontends (**Services ▸ HAProxy ▸ Settings ▸ Virtual Services ▸ Public Services**, plugin `os-haproxy`).



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) UUID of the frontend.

### Read-Only

- `advertised_protocols` (Set of String) When using the TLS ALPN extension, HAProxy advertises the specified protocol list as supported on top of ALPN. SSL offloading must be enabled. Note that HTTP/3 will only be added to QUIC-compatible Listening Addresses. One of `h3`, `h2`, `http11`, `http10`.
- `basic_auth_enabled` (Boolean) Enable HTTP Basic Authentication.
- `basic_auth_groups` (Set of String) Allowed Groups.
- `basic_auth_users` (Set of String) Allowed Users.
- `bind` (Set of String) Configure listen addresses for this Public Service, i.e. 127.0.0.1:8080 or www.example.com:443 or unix@socket-name. Add quic4@ or quic6@ to enable QUIC for IPv4/IPv6, e.g. quic4@www.example.com:443. Use TAB key to complete typing a listen address.
- `bind_options` (String) A list of parameters that will be appended to every Listen Address line.Example: accept-proxy npn http/1.1.
- `connection_behaviour` (String) By default HAProxy operates in keep-alive mode with regards to persistent connections. Option "httpclose" configures HAProxy to close connections with the server and the client as soon as the request and the response are received. It will also check if a "Connection: close" header is already set in each direction, and will add one if missing. Option "http-server-close" enables HTTP connection-close mode on the server side while keeping the ability to support HTTP keep-alive and pipelining on the client side. One of `http-keep-alive`, `httpclose`, `http-server-close`.
- `custom_options` (String) These lines will be added to the HAProxy frontend configuration.
- `default_backend` (String) Set the default Backend Pool to use for this Public Service.
- `description` (String) Description for this Public Service.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable this Public Service.
- `forward_for` (Boolean) This option is deprecated and should no longer be used. A new option is available in backend pool settings.
- `http2_enabled` (Boolean) Enable support for HTTP/2.
- `http2_enabled_nontls` (Boolean) Enable support for HTTP/2 even if TLS (SSL offloading) is not enabled.
- `linked_actions` (Set of String) Choose rules to be included in this Public Service.
- `linked_cpu_affinity_rules` (Set of String) Choose CPU affinity rules that should be applied to this Public Service.
- `linked_errorfiles` (Set of String) Choose error messages to be included in this Public Service.
- `logging_detailed_log` (Boolean) Enable or disable verbose logging. Each log line turns into a much richer format.
- `logging_dont_log_normal` (Boolean) Enable or disable logging of normal, successful connections.
- `logging_dont_log_null` (Boolean) Enable or disable logging of connections with no data.
- `logging_log_separate_errors` (Boolean) Allow HAProxy to automatically raise log level for non-completely successful connections to aid debugging.
- `logging_socket_stats` (Boolean) Enable or disable collecting & providing separate statistics for each socket.
- `mode` (String) Set the running mode or protocol for this Public Service. One of `http`, `ssl`, `tcp`.
- `name` (String) Name to identify this Public Service.
- `prometheus_enabled` (Boolean) Enable HAProxy's Prometheus exporter.
- `prometheus_path` (String) The path where the Prometheus exporter can be accessed.
- `ssl_advanced_enabled` (Boolean) Enable advanced SSL settings.
- `ssl_bind_options` (Set of String) Used to enforce or disable certain SSL options. One of `no-sslv3`, `no-tlsv10`, `no-tlsv11`, `no-tlsv12`, `no-tlsv13`, `no-tls-tickets`, `force-sslv3`, `force-tlsv10`, `force-tlsv11`, `force-tlsv12`, `force-tlsv13`, `prefer-client-ciphers`, `strict-sni`.
- `ssl_certificates` (Set of String) Select certificates to use for SSL offloading. HAProxy's SNI recognition will determine the correct certificate automatically. If no SNI is provided by the client then the first certificate will be presented.To import additional certificates, go to Certificate Manager.
- `ssl_cipher_list` (String) It sets the default string describing the list of cipher algorithms ("cipher suite") that are negotiated during the SSL/TLS handshake up to TLSv1.2.
- `ssl_cipher_suites` (String) It sets the default string describing the list of cipher algorithms ("cipher suite") that are negotiated during the SSL/TLS handshake for TLSv1.3.
- `ssl_client_auth_cas` (Set of String) Select CA certificates to use for client certificate authentication. To import additional CAs, go to CA Manager.
- `ssl_client_auth_crls` (Set of String) Select CRLs to use for client certificate authentication. To import additional CRLs, go to CRL Manager.
- `ssl_client_auth_enabled` (Boolean) Enable Client Certificate Authentication.
- `ssl_client_auth_verify` (String) If set to 'optional' or 'required', client certificate is requested. One of `none`, `optional`, `required`.
- `ssl_custom_options` (String) Pass additional SSL parameters to the HAProxy configuration.
- `ssl_default_certificate` (String) This certificate will be presented if no SNI is provided by the client or if the client provides an SNI hostname which does not match any certificate. This parameter is optional to enforce a certain sort order for certificates.
- `ssl_enabled` (Boolean) Enable SSL offloading.
- `ssl_hsts_enabled` (Boolean) Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security.
- `ssl_hsts_include_sub_domains` (Boolean) Enable if all present and future subdomains will be HTTPS.
- `ssl_hsts_max_age` (Number) Future requests to the domain should use only HTTPS for the specified time (in seconds): 15768000 = 6 months.
- `ssl_hsts_preload` (Boolean) Enable if you like this domain to be included in the HSTS preload list.
- `ssl_max_version` (String) This option enforces use of the specified version (or lower) on SSL connections. One of `SSLv3`, `TLSv1.0`, `TLSv1.1`, `TLSv1.2`, `TLSv1.3`.
- `ssl_min_version` (String) This option enforces use of the specified version (or higher) on SSL connections. One of `SSLv3`, `TLSv1.0`, `TLSv1.1`, `TLSv1.2`, `TLSv1.3`.
- `stickiness_bytes_in_rate_period` (String) The length of the period over which the average is measured. It reports the average incoming bytes rate over that period, in bytes per period. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `stickiness_bytes_out_rate_period` (String) The length of the period over which the average is measured. It reports the average outgoing bytes rate over that period, in bytes per period. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `stickiness_conn_rate_period` (String) The length of the period over which the average is measured. It reports the average incoming connection rate over that period, in connections per period. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `stickiness_counter` (Boolean) Enable to be able to retrieve values from sticky counters. If disabled, all values will return 0, rendering many conditions useless.
- `stickiness_counter_key` (String) It describes what elements of the incoming request or connection will be analyzed, extracted, combined, and used to select which table entry to update the counters. Defaults to "src" to track elements of the source IP. See the HAProxy documentation for a full description.
- `stickiness_data_types` (Set of String) This is used to store additional information in the stick-table. It may be used by ACLs in order to control various criteria related to the activity of the client matching the stick-table. Note that this directly impacts memory usage. See the HAProxy documentation for a full description. One of `bytes_in_cnt`, `bytes_in_rate`, `bytes_out_cnt`, `bytes_out_rate`, `conn_cnt`, `conn_cur`, `conn_rate`, `glitch_cnt`, `glitch_rate`, `gpc`, `gpc_rate`, `gpc0`, `gpc0_rate`, `gpc1`, `gpc1_rate`, `gpt`, `gpt0`, `http_err_cnt`, `http_err_rate`, `http_fail_cnt`, `http_fail_rate`, `http_req_cnt`, `http_req_rate`, `server_id`, `sess_cnt`, `sess_rate`.
- `stickiness_expire` (String) Enter a number followed by one of the supported suffixes "d" (days), "h" (hour), "m" (minute), "s" (seconds), "ms" (miliseconds). This configures the maximum duration of an entry in the stick-table since it was last created, refreshed or matched. The maximum duration is slightly above 24 days.
- `stickiness_glitch_rate_period` (String) The length of the period over which the average is measured. It reports the average front glitches rate over that period. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `stickiness_gpc_elements` (Number) The number of array elements that will be used for the General Purpose Counter. This is limited to a maximum of 100 elements, ranging from 0 to 99.
- `stickiness_gpc_rate_period` (String) The length of the period over which the average is measured. Most of the time it will be used to measure the frequency of occurrence of certain events. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `stickiness_gpt_elements` (Number) The number of array elements that will be used for the General Purpose Tag. This is limited to a maximum of 100 elements, ranging from 0 to 99.
- `stickiness_http_err_rate_period` (String) The length of the period over which the average is measured. It reports the average HTTP request error rate over that period, in requests per period. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `stickiness_http_fail_rate_period` (String) The length of the period over which the average is measured. It reports the average HTTP response fail error rate over that period, in requests per period. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `stickiness_http_req_rate_period` (String) The length of the period over which the average is measured. It reports the average HTTP request rate over that period, in requests per period. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `stickiness_length` (Number) Specify the maximum length for a value in the stick-table. If the value is larger than this value it will be truncated before being stored. Depending on the stick-table type this repesents either characters or bytes.
- `stickiness_pattern` (String) Choose the type of data that should be stored in this stick-table. Note that this stick-table cannot be used for session persistence, it is only used to store additional per-connection data (select below). See the HAProxy documentation for further information. One of `binary`, `integer`, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `string`.
- `stickiness_sess_rate_period` (String) The length of the period over which the average is measured. It reports the average incoming session rate over that period, in sessions per period. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `stickiness_size` (String) Enter a number followed by one of the supported suffixes "k", "m", "g". This configures the maximum number of entries that can fit in the table. This value directly impacts memory usage. Count approximately 50 bytes per entry, plus the size of a string if any.
- `tuning_max_connections` (Number) Set the maximum number of concurrent connections for this Public Service.
- `tuning_shards` (Number) This option automatically creates the specified number of listeners for every IP:port combination and evenly distributes them among available threads. This can sometimes be useful when using very large thread counts where the in-kernel locking on a single socket starts to cause a significant overhead.
- `tuning_timeout_client` (String) Set the maximum inactivity time on the client side. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `tuning_timeout_http_keep_alive` (String) Set the maximum allowed time to wait for a new HTTP request to appear. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
- `tuning_timeout_http_req` (String) Set the maximum allowed time to wait for a complete HTTP request. In order to offer DoS protection, it may be required to lower the maximum accepted time to receive a complete HTTP request without affecting the client timeout. This helps protecting against established connections on which nothing is sent. Defaults to milliseconds. Optionally the unit may be specified as either "d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or "us".
